extracted.intended_audience: readers of wire-service international news and policymakers interested in post‑World War II diplomacy and German economic policy
extracted.subtask_description: A historical wire-service news article reporting on international diplomacy (Council of Foreign Ministers) and related postwar developments (Germany economic proposals, Ruhr control, reparations) alongside Middle East/Palestine violence reports. Primarily a factual report of statements, demands and events.

rubrics_metrics.name: Four-power control of the Ruhr
rubrics_metrics.description: Molotov listed four‑Power control of the Ruhr and repeal of the economic merger of the American and British zones as part of the price of Soviet agreement to unify Germany.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Under the central economic organization he proposed, the Ruhr industrial region would be placed under joint control of the United Kingdom, France, the United States and the U.S.S.R.; this is presented as a Soviet precondition for agreement on German unification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Veto rights for zonal commanders in central economic organization
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the central economic organization he proposed, each of the four zonal commanders could veto any decision of the central body.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The veto mechanism is specified as part of Molotov's plan for central economic organization, giving each zone commander the right to block central decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reparations: form and duration
rubrics_metrics.description: The Soviet Minister declared that war damages should be paid over twenty years in industrial equipment, German assets abroad and various services and current production.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Molotov reiterated Soviet demands for reparations (a $10,000,000,000 figure is mentioned elsewhere in the coverage) and tied reparations to the form of deliveries (equipment, assets, services) and an extended payment period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prevent restoration of Germany's war industrial potential
rubrics_metrics.description: Objectives for rehabilitation 'shall be pursued with due regard to the interests of security and to preventing the restoration of Germany's war industry.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Molotov accuses Anglo‑American actions of restoring war industrial potential and argues rehabilitation must avoid reconstituting military capability; this is a guiding constraint on acceptable economic measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish central German administrative departments under quadripartite supervision
rubrics_metrics.description: The Control Council is directed to set up at the earliest possible moment central German administrative departments dealing with matters calling for centralized decisions (food, agriculture, etc.). Central German administrative departments will be under the supervision and direction of the appropriate quadripartite agencies of the Allied Control Authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These central departments are to handle nationwide functions while remaining supervised by four‑Power allied agencies; intended to coordinate rehabilitation across zones.

rubrics_metrics.name: Zone commanders' supervisory and suspension authority
rubrics_metrics.description: The zone commanders, each in their own zone, shall exercise general supervision and control over the activities of central German departments. In cases where directives of the central German administration contravene directives of the Control Council, the zone commanders shall, after informing the Control Council, have the right to suspend execution of such directives; the Control Council will make the final decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines a procedural check: zone commanders may suspend contested central directives pending a Control Council decision, preserving four‑power oversight and dispute resolution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Target annual steel output level
rubrics_metrics.description: Provisions are made 'so as to bring the annual output of steel to 10,000,000 to 12,000,000 tons at an early date.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A specific quantitative rehabilitation target is stipulated for steel production as part of economic recovery planning; central departments are responsible for measures to reach this level, but within the limits set to prevent rearmament.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nationwide financial and monetary reform
rubrics_metrics.description: Action on a nation‑wide basis shall be taken to reform the financial and monetary system in Germany.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Molotov calls for monetary/financial reform implemented across all zones (implying four‑power coordination) rather than unilateral zone changes that could partition Germany economically.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expand German exports to insure imports and reparations
rubrics_metrics.description: In order to insure imports of raw materials and other materials necessary for German peacetime industry and the discharge by Germany of her obligations to the Allies, the expansion of German exports shall be ensured.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Economic rehabilitation must include measures to increase exports so Germany can import necessary inputs and meet reparations obligations; implies policy measures to facilitate export growth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restore interzonal trade; abolish zonal economic agencies
rubrics_metrics.description: When central German departments have been set up and the procedure for fulfillment of the ... obligations has been decided, interzonal economic trade and the necessary facilities provided for the free flow of goods throughout all Germany. All zonal German economic agencies covering one or more zones shall also be abolished.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Molotov demands restoration of economic unity and removal of administrative barriers between zones, eliminating separate zonal economic bodies in favor of centralized, four‑power supervised structures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nullify Anglo‑American agreements that contravene Germany's economic unity
rubrics_metrics.description: The agreement concerning the economic unification of the British and American zones as well ... Separate agreements connected with this unification shall be deemed null and void as contravening the economic unity of Germany.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Soviet position rejects Western unilateral unification actions (e.g., Anglo‑American zone merger) and seeks their invalidation on grounds they violate four‑power economic unity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid use of former Nazi industrialists and monopolists in rehabilitation
rubrics_metrics.description: The Anglo‑American authorities, by separate action, are carrying through their decision concerning the one‑sided restoration of certain branches of heavy industry, for instance the steel industry, drawing old Hitlerite circles of industrial monopolists and trusts to take part in these enterprises.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Molotov criticizes Western rehabilitation for relying on ex‑Nazi industrial elites; implication is that rehabilitation policy should exclude those elements to prevent revival of militarist networks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Central departments to frame rehabilitation measures within new industry limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Central German departments shall be responsible for framing measures for the rehabilitation of the German economy within the limits of the new level of industry, Germany being bound to fulfill unconditionally the reparation and other basic obligations imposed upon her.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rehabilitation planning must respect a defined 'new level' of industry (a ceiling to prevent remilitarization) while ensuring Germany meets reparations and other obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unified currency under four‑power control; oppose unilateral zone currency changes
rubrics_metrics.description: American leaders have opposed any currency change in western Germany alone on the ground ... From a single set of plates in Berlin under four‑power control ... negotiations broke down on the Russian proposition that part of the money printed under Russian control ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article records opposition to unilateral currency reform in a single zone and indicates a Soviet preference for a unified currency issued under four‑power control to avoid partition‑by‑currency and unilateral advantage.
